children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Thursday.
WHEAT - Down 9 to 12 cents per bushel
ease on technical selling and weaker crude oil prices. Losses limited by continued worries about disruptions of Black Sea grain exports.

Actively traded CBOT December wheat (WZ26) hit overhead chart resistance at its 20-day moving average during overnight trading, a level that the contract has failed to break through for four straight sessions.
Russia has damaged a bridge in the Odesa region, significantly limiting Ukraine's ability to transport grain to its Danube river ports, Ukraine's state railway operator said on Thursday.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said net U.S. wheat export sales in the week ended September 10 totaled 325,900 metric tons for shipment in the 2026/27 marketing year, in line with trade estimates.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 10 cents at $7.20-3/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 9 cents at $7.90-1/2 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 7 cents at $7.49 a bushel.
CORN - Down 2 to 4 cents per bushel
futures weaker on lower crude oil prices and a looming U.S. Midwest harvest.
The USDA reported net U.S. corn export sales last week at 1,026,700 metric tons for shipment in the 2026/27 marketing year, near the low end of a range of trade estimates.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 2-3/4 cents at $5.31-1/2 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 1 to 3 cents per bushel
ease on technical selling after three sessions of gains. Expectations for Chinese buying ahead of a meeting between presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump next week underpinned the market.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend ahead of next week's Trump-Xi meeting.
The USDA said net U.S. soybean export sales in the week ended September 10 totaled 1,702,000 metric tons for shipment in the 2026/27 marketing year, in line with trade estimates.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 1-1/2 cents at $13.19 per bushel.
